title: An overview of SoapUI and legacy SOAP services

videos.script: Some of the services you will test were written twenty years ago. They speak SOAP. {{envelope}} SOAP puts every request inside an envelope of XML. Every envelope goes to the same address, by POST. {{one-address}} The address names the service. What to do is written inside the message. The contract comes with it. It is called a WSDL, and the service usually serves it itself. {{wsdl}} You will meet SOAP in tax systems, banks and insurers. Often it sits behind the API you are actually testing. In this lesson you run a small invoice service of your own and call it with curl. {{curl}} You will read its faults. A fault says who was to blame, the client or the server. {{fault}} One of its faults blames the wrong side. You will find it, and write a test that stays red until it is fixed. {{test}} Then a look at SoapUI, the tool built for all of this. It could not run here, so its screens are described in words. By the end you can call a SOAP service, assert on its answer, and read a WSDL.
